title: Yield curve 101
label: The yield curve shows how much it costs the
federal government to borrow money for a given
amount of time, revealing the relationship
between long- and short-term interest rates.
It is, inherently, a forecast for what the
economy holds in the future — how much
inflation there will be, for example, and how
healthy growth will be over the years ahead —
all embodied in the price of money today,
tomorrow and many years from now.

title: Lowest 10-year yield: July 2012
label: The 10-year yield averaged 1.53 percent in
July 2012. On July 25 it closed at 1.43
percent.
